newsitem.title: ROMANIA: VIRAL MENINGITIS OUTBREAK KILLS 20 IN ROMANIA.
newsitem.headline: VIRAL MENINGITIS OUTBREAK KILLS 20 IN ROMANIA.

text.p: The death toll in Romania's worst viral meningitis outbreak in a decade has risen to 20, health ministry sources said on Monday.
A ministry statement said on Monday the dead were from a total of 380 patients hospitalised across Romania, the majority of them in Bucharest. Most of the dead were elderly.
It said there were 45 new cases over the weekend, but declined to describe the situation as an "epidemic".
Health Minister Daniela Bartos said last week that the number of cases was still small and "under international standards, it could not be called an epidemic".

The contamination has apparently been caused by tourists returning from Cyprus. More than 100 people fell ill with mild meningitis in the southern coastal town of Limassol, centre of Cyprus's tourist trade, in July.
Illness from viral meningitis lasts around a week. It affects the gastro-intestinal tract, causing high fever, headache and vomiting.
Some 50 children have been affected and health authorities said some schools with poor sanitation may be banned from reopening after the summer break to prevent the disease's spread.
Emergency inspections found 14 schools in the capital had no running water.
In 1986 Romania suffered an epidemic of the more dangerous bacterial meningitis which has killed some 15,000 people in central Africa this year.
